subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Jet Engine: How It Actually Works
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Jet Engine: How It Actually Works usable.

hook.text: A jet engine does four things: suck, squeeze, bang, blow. That's the entire cycle in four words.

buildup.text: Air enters the intake. The compressor squeezes it to 30 times atmospheric pressure. Fuel is injected and ignited.

discovery.text: Hot gases expand through the turbine, spinning the compressor. Remaining energy exits as high-speed exhaust — creating thrust.

twist.text: Frank Whittle patented the turbojet in 1930 but couldn't get funding. Germany's Hans von Ohain flew a jet first in 1939.

climax.text: Modern turbofans bypass most air around the core. They're quieter and more fuel-efficient than pure turbojets.

punchline.text: Suck. Squeeze. Bang. Blow. Four steps. Forty thousand pounds of thrust.

quiz.question: Who first patented the turbojet engine concept?
options: The Wright brothers included a jet design in their original aircraft patent
Frank Whittle patented it in 1930, though Germany flew a jet engine first
Hans von Ohain both invented and first flew the jet engine in Germany
